**Assessment/Plan:**

• **Stroke (CVA)**: Ms. Stanley's last cerebrovascular accident occurred 28.5 years ago. She is currently stable and under control. The patient is taking **atorvastatin 20 mg** daily, which has been effective in managing her cholesterol levels and reducing the risk of recurrent strokes.

• **Epilepsy / seizure disorder**: Ms. Stanley has been diagnosed with epilepsy for almost a decade, with approximately eight seizures per year. She has been seizure-free for 15.1 years. Her current medications include **phenytoin 100 mg** and **topiramate 50 mg**, which are being well-tolerated and have effectively controlled her seizure activity. A recent EEG showed no epileptiform activity.

• **Back Strain**: Ms. Stanley has had multiple episodes of back strain over the past year. She has been advised on proper lifting techniques and exercises to strengthen her back muscles. She has been prescribed physical therapy, which she has been attending regularly. The latest visit showed improvement in her range of motion and reduced pain levels.

• **Hypertension**: Ms. Stanley's blood pressure has remained within a normal range during her visits, although she has been advised to maintain a diet low in sodium and engage in regular physical activity to keep her cardiovascular health in check.

• **Alcohol Consumption**: Ms. Stanley reports consuming approximately eight drinks per week, which we have discussed as a potential factor for her seizure disorder. We advised her to consider reducing her alcohol intake to minimize any potential impact on her seizure control.
